operationalization: Compare landmark Procrustes distances of octanol-treated Girardia dorotocephala regenerates with water-treated controls and with wild-type heads of the named other species, and score whether the same individuals later return to the Girardia shape without a species-diagnostic genotype change. Support would be treated heads falling inside the other species' shape clusters and later leaving them; a continuous rounding that never matches those clusters, or a required genetic change, would weaken the result.

candidate_datasets.name: TimeTree
candidate_datasets.role: divergence-time estimates among the named planarian lineages for the 100–150 million year clause

candidate_datasets.name: Emmons-Bell et al. 2015, International Journal of Molecular Sciences
candidate_datasets.role: published landmark morphometrics, canonical variates and images of octanol-treated versus species-typical heads

candidate_datasets.name: PlanMine
candidate_datasets.role: reference transcriptomes of the named species, not expression profiles of the treated fragments

obstacles: Landmark coordinates are not deposited, so a reanalysis has to be digitized from the published images.
Octanol is not a gap-junction-specific reagent, and rounded heads can form a continuum rather than discrete species attractors.
Treated animals were not sequenced, so absence of genetic change is inferred from wild-type parentage.
rationale: An open morphometric study reports canonical variates for more than sixty worms and describes later remodeling, and public divergence times can check the phylogenetic-distance clause. The coordinate file itself is not downloadable, and there is no independent raw archive or sequence check of the altered animals. Shape similarity can therefore be re-examined only in part, and the attractor wording is not separated from a graded wound response.

operationalization: In polyploid versus diploid newt embryos, count cells per pronephric-tubule cross-section, measure cell cross-sectional area, and measure lumen diameter, including the extreme in which one cell forms the wall. Matched diameter with fewer, larger cells would support size compensation; diameter scaling in proportion to cell size, or no single-cell tubules, would refute that part. Calling the match a switch among molecular mechanisms, or an anatomical goal, needs a separate assay the anatomy does not contain.
obstacles: The counts and drawings are in a 1945 journal article and later retellings, not a downloadable table or image stack.
Cell size was changed by ploidy, which also changes nuclear content, so mechanism switching is not isolated.
The sample is newt pronephric tubules, not kidney tubules in general.
rationale: Cell number, cell size and tubule diameter are standard variables, and the classic paper reports the compensation down to a single curved cell. Those measurements are not in any open repository, so a check means recovering mid-century plates rather than running a deposited table. The anatomical pattern can be scrutinized from that literature; the further claim that different molecular pathways are recruited to meet a goal is not in those plates.

operationalization: From the published movies and counts, score whether motile Xenopus ectoderm spheroids gather loose cells into piles that compact into further motile spheroids, and record the time from assembly to the first offspring. Offspring that swim and themselves pile cells would support kinematic replication on the reported timescale; piles that never become autonomous movers, or a requirement for a long selection history, would weaken it. A survey of other species is a separate test and is not in this archive.

candidate_datasets.name: Kriegman et al. 2021, PNAS
candidate_datasets.role: published counts and supplementary movies of pile formation and offspring motility; the paper states that the non-code data are in the manuscript and supplement

candidate_datasets.name: Kinematically replicating organisms source code
candidate_datasets.role: public simulation and design code for the kinematic-replication model, not the wet-lab cell tracks

obstacles: The public code re-runs the design simulation; it does not replace the Petri-dish counts.
Pile formation can be passive flow-driven aggregation rather than construction of a copy.
No public survey tests the claim that no other species uses this mode.
rationale: The replication paper puts its counts and movies in the open supplement and releases the simulation code, so the reported Xenopus time course can be re-measured and the model re-run. That does not deposit raw offspring coordinates, and it does not contain a comparative survey of other species. The biological phenotype is therefore only partly checkable, and the simulation does not adjudicate the wet-lab result.

operationalization: Using the published 32-landmark scheme, compute Procrustes distance of scrambled versus unperturbed tadpoles to the normal frog-face configuration at successive ages, separately for jaws, branchial arches, eyes, nostrils and otoliths. Convergence of scrambled animals onto the control region along trajectories that normal animals do not follow would support the claim; persistent separation, or correction of only some structures, would restrict it.

candidate_datasets.name: Vandenberg, Adams and Levin 2012, Developmental Dynamics
candidate_datasets.role: published geometric-morphometric landmarks, canonical variates and age series for scrambled Xenopus craniofacial anatomy

candidate_datasets.name: Xenbase
candidate_datasets.role: standard Xenopus staging and craniofacial anatomy used to define a normal face, not the perturbation coordinate file

obstacles: Landmark coordinates are published as analyses, not as a downloadable coordinate table.
Age-binned group averages do not reconstruct individual paths through morphospace.
Jaws and branchial arches are scored separately from eyes, nostrils and otoliths, so one face-wide goal region is an extra summary.
rationale: The primary study is a public geometric morphometric series with a defined landmark scheme and canonical variate tests across months of tadpole life. Without the coordinate file, a new worker can re-read the published separations but cannot recompute individual trajectories. The data can test return toward normal for some structures in this one species, and they are weaker for a single shared goal region reached by new paths.

operationalization: In mosaic channel misexpression with a lineage label, measure the fraction of unlabeled host cells inside ectopic tail lenses and plot lens diameter against the number of channel-positive cells. A normal-sized lens built mostly from unlabeled cells, after only a few labeled cells expressed the channel, would support recruitment; lenses composed only of the labeled clone, or size scaling with clone size, would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: Pai et al. 2012, Development
candidate_datasets.role: published lineage-labeled ectopic lens and eye images in Xenopus, including tail sites, with incidence counts

candidate_datasets.name: Xenbase
candidate_datasets.role: Xenopus phenotype and gene records linked to the eye-induction experiments, not cell-by-cell contribution counts

obstacles: The published lineage result reports ectopic tissue as label-positive and does not tabulate an unlabeled host fraction.
Normal lens diameter is not plotted against the number of channel-expressing cells.
A minority of injected cells forming eye tissue is a different measurement from those cells recruiting neighbors.
rationale: Ectopic tail lens tissue after voltage perturbation, and a lineage label on the injected cells, are in an open paper with incidence counts. That paper's sections argue the labeled cells themselves took on eye identity, and it does not publish the host-cell fraction or a size-versus-clone curve the recruitment wording needs. Existing images can constrain the claim; they do not carry the cell-contribution table that would settle it.

operationalization: Dye coupling and calcium imaging can show that small cytosolic signals cross gap junctions. The same images are predicted if calcium simply diffuses and if a cell 'cannot tell' which molecule is its own, so ownership, erasure of cellular individuality, and scaling of stored goals have no separate confirming or refuting observation.
obstacles: Any shared calcium transient fits both passive coupling and an ownership-wiping description.
Individuality and stored goals are not given a measurement distinct from the coupling itself.
rationale: Cytosolic continuity through gap junctions is a routine physiological observation, and many imaging papers already show it. Nothing in those records distinguishes loss of molecular ownership, partial erasure of cell identity, or scaling of goals from ordinary diffusion of a second messenger. The distinctive content of the statement therefore has no empirical contrast with the non-cognitive description of the same facts.

operationalization: Start from single dissociated adult normal human bronchial epithelial cells, culture them in matrix for two weeks, move the products to low-viscosity medium, and score multicellularity and motility without added genes, scaffolds or sculpting. Clonal spheroids that translocate would support the protocol result; aggregates that require many seed cells, or that remain immotile, would refute the single-cell self-construction claim.
obstacles: The paper states that the supporting data are available from the authors on request, not in a public archive.
Supplementary videos illustrate motility; they do not show that each spheroid began as one cell.
Donor and batch replication counts are not in an open table.
rationale: Single-cell origin, multicellularity and motility are ordinary counts and tracks. The 2024 paper's own data-availability statement keeps the underlying measurements with the authors, and the public videos are illustrations rather than the cohort. Checking the result means a new run of the protocol or release of the withheld logs, not analysis of an existing open file.

operationalization: Apply the same no-edit self-assembly assay to adult somatic human cells and to additional wild-type cell types beyond frog embryonic ectoderm, and score whether a novel motile anatomy appears. One repeated adult-human success would support the narrower contrast with amphibian embryos; failure across further wild-type types would refute the claim that the plasticity is a general feature of wild-type cells.

candidate_datasets.name: Xenobots behavioral data and analysis code
candidate_datasets.role: public tracks for the frog embryonic constructs used as the amphibian baseline, not for adult human cells

obstacles: Adult human assembly measurements are author-on-request, so the new half of the contrast is not open.
Two epithelial systems cannot separate a general wild-type capacity from a property of ciliated epithelia.
What counts as a novel functional anatomy has to be fixed before the universal wording is testable.
rationale: Open Xenobot tracks document novel behavior in frog embryonic cells, which is the baseline this statement says the phenomenon exceeds. The adult human half, and any broader sample of wild-type cell types, is not in a public dataset. A decisive test of the generalization still requires new cell-type runs or release of the Anthrobot cohort.

operationalization: Live-image basal and apical markers from the moment spheroids leave Matrigel until cilia are external, and test whether basal cells move inward rather than apical cells moving outward or new cilia differentiating in place. Inward basal migration that precedes external cilia would support the viscosity hypothesis; polarity reversal without basal displacement would refute that particular route.
obstacles: Endpoint stains at day 0 and day 7 do not track which cells moved.
Viscosity is changed by leaving the gel, which also changes adhesion and ligand presentation.
The cell-resolution movies that would separate the routes are not deposited.
rationale: Basal-cell position over time is a measurable variable, and the paper states the inward-migration route as a hypothesis tied to viscosity. Public material, if any, is endpoint immunostaining, which is compatible with several rearrangements. Distinguishing inward basal migration from other polarity switches needs new live imaging or a deposited tracking set that does not exist.

operationalization: Score the fraction of apical-in spheroids that translocate on day 0 and on day 7 after release into low-adhesive liquid culture, and count external multiciliated cells by acetylated-tubulin staining at the same times. A rise in both motility and external cilia would support the time course; motility without external cilia, or no change by day 7, would refute it.
obstacles: Motility counts and cilia tallies are in figures and are not a deposited table.
Day-7 staining is a separate sample from the tracked spheroids, so the pairing is by cohort rather than by individual.
The public videos are examples, not the every-other-day census.
rationale: Motile fraction and external cilia counts are direct variables with an obvious contrast between day 0 and day 7. The paper reports that contrast and places the underlying data with the authors on request. Re-inspecting the published panels is not a reanalysis of the census, so the test waits on the raw counts or a new culture run.

operationalization: Compare diameter and motile fraction of Anthrobots grown above the protocol viscosity with baseline low-viscosity cultures, holding seeding density fixed. Lower motility and smaller size at higher viscosity would support the reported effect; no change, or a size change without a motility change, would weaken the joint claim.
obstacles: The viscosity series is in supporting figures, with the measurements available on request.
Raising matrix concentration changes biochemical cues as well as viscosity.
The number of bots and the viscosity values are not in an open table.
rationale: Size and motile fraction versus culture viscosity are straightforward endpoints. They appear as supporting figures whose underlying values were not deposited. A retest needs those values or a new viscosity series; the public record does not contain a downloadable size and motility table.

operationalization: At 15,000, 30,000 and 60,000 cells per millilitre, record final bot diameter and the day-by-day motile fraction. A significant, non-linear shift in both size and the motility time course would support seeding density as a control parameter; overlapping size distributions, or a strictly linear response, would refute the stated pattern.
obstacles: Three-density size and motility curves are not deposited.
Density also changes nutrient and oxygen competition, so it is not a pure morphological knob.
Non-linearity is hard to establish from three points without the raw replicates.
rationale: Seeding density, diameter and motile fraction are all measured quantities, and the paper describes half, default and double density. Those curves remain with the authors. Without the replicate table, the significance and the non-linear shape cannot be recomputed from open data.

operationalization: Count motile spheroids every other day for three weeks after matrix dissolution, fit the motile fraction against time, and ask whether the largest step falls on day 10 and whether external cilia increase on the same schedule. A sigmoidal fit with the steepest step at day 10, matched by cilia exposure, would support the time course; a linear rise, a different peak day, or motility without added surface cilia, would refute it.
obstacles: The every-other-day counts behind the sigmoidal plot are not deposited.
Cilia staining is reported at day 0 and day 7, not at the day-10 step.
A curve fit to one cohort does not separate maturation from selective survival of motile bots.
rationale: A motile-fraction time series and a cilia stain are enough, in principle, to test both the sigmoidal timing and the reorganization clause. The census is figure-only and held on request, and the cilia comparison does not sample the day of steepest change. Confirming or refuting the fitted time course requires the count table or a new time series.

operationalization: Measure speed before and after ciliobrevin, with a vehicle control, on the same bots. A sharp drop that reverses the way ciliary beat stops, and that spares non-ciliary readouts, would support cilia-driven locomotion; unchanged speed would refute it.
obstacles: The ciliobrevin speeds are in a supporting figure and are not deposited.
Ciliobrevin inhibits cytoplasmic dynein, so a motility drop is not cilia-exclusive without a beat assay on the same bots.
Dose, sample size and the pre-drug baseline are not in an open table.
rationale: A paired speed change under a cilia-motion blocker is a direct test of how these bots move. The paper reports a drastic decrease and does not release the tracks. The pharmacological contrast is clean enough to be decisive once the numbers exist in public form; they do not yet.

operationalization: Recompute straightness and gyration on the 30-second segments from the roughly 200 tracked bots and repeat the unsupervised clustering under the original and under alternative cluster counts. Four groups that align with circular, linear, curvilinear and mixed paths, and that are preferred by a stability criterion, would support discrete types; a continuous cloud or a different preferred count would refute four types.
obstacles: Trajectory coordinates for the 200 bots are not public.
Four clusters can be imposed by the choice of k and by the two indices.
Example videos show one bot of each narrated type, not the sample used for clustering.
rationale: Straightness, gyration and a cluster-number criterion are a fully specified reanalysis, and they would separate discrete types from a continuum if the tracks existed. The paper keeps those coordinates on request. Watching representative clips does not rerun the clustering, so the four-type partition is not resolvable from open data.

operationalization: From labeled 30-second segments, estimate the Markov transition matrix among circular, linear, curvilinear and eclectic states over the five-hour recordings. Circular self-transition highest, and eclectic outflow into the other three states, would support the stability order; a high eclectic self-transition, or frequent circular-to-linear switches, would refute it.
obstacles: Segment labels and the transition counts are not deposited.
The eclectic class is defined as whatever is left over, so its role as an intermediate is partly by construction.
Stability ranks inherit whatever cluster boundaries were chosen upstream.
rationale: A transition matrix among movement labels is a standard calculation and would rank persistence if the segment labels were public. They are not. The result also depends on the unpublished clustering step, so neither the rank order nor the intermediate status of eclectic motion can be recomputed now.

operationalization: For each bot, compute the fraction of its 30-second segments that stay in one movement class and the rate of switches between circular and linear. High within-bot consistency and rare cross-class switches would support stable individual types; frequent switching by the same bot would refute a lasting fingerprint. Separating active self-organization from a type fixed by the initial cilia pattern needs early-time tracks the consistency score alone does not provide.
obstacles: Per-bot identity of segments is not in a public file.
Low switching does not distinguish self-organization from a type fixed at release by cilia geometry.
A fingerprint is only as discrete as the upstream cluster boundaries.
rationale: Within-bot consistency is measurable from the same five-hour tracks as the transition matrix, and those tracks are not public. Even with them, rare switching would not show that bots self-organize into types rather than simply keeping the geometry they had when recording started. The stability half is waiting on data; the self-organization wording stays underdetermined.

operationalization: On the confocal cohort, compare cilia-coverage fraction and a polarization index across the three morphotypes. Morphotype 2 higher on coverage, and morphotype 3 higher on polarization with fewer isolated patches, would support the contrasts; overlapping distributions would refute them.
obstacles: Cilia masks and the eight indices for the roughly 350 bots are not deposited.
Polarization and coverage are correlated with size, which also defines the types.
Significance depends on how the three groups were cut.
rationale: Coverage and polarization are explicit image measurements, and the paper reports both contrasts as significant. The feature table from the confocal cohort was not released. Re-running the group tests requires that table or a new imaging set; the published summary plot is not enough to recompute the differences.

operationalization: Repeat principal-component analysis and clustering on the eight shape and cilia indices, and compare a three-group solution with two- and four-group solutions by a pre-specified criterion. A stable split of small smooth spheres from larger irregular bots, and a further cilia-pattern split of the large bots, would support the decision tree; a continuum or a different first split would refute three morphotypes in that order.
obstacles: The eight-index matrix is not public.
Three clusters and a tree order are sensitive to scaling and to the choice of k.
Size and shape are partly the same measurement, so the first split can be a size threshold.
rationale: The morphotype tree is a clustering claim about a defined feature set of about 350 bots. That matrix is not deposited, and cluster count is method-dependent even when the matrix exists. Open figures do not let a third party rerun the principal components or test whether three groups are preferred.

operationalization: Cross-tabulate movement class against morphotype for the imaged bots, including the 28 with an assigned displacing type, and repeat the Fisher exact test. Enrichment of non-movers in type 1, linear movers in type 2 and circular movers in type 3, with no displacing bot in type 1, would support the mapping; a flat table would refute it.
obstacles: The bot-level behavior and morphotype labels are not deposited.
Only 28 of about 350 imaged bots carried a displacing movement label.
Movement type and morphotype were both derived by the same investigators, so the overlap inherits both classification choices.
rationale: A Fisher test on a behavior-by-morphotype table is a standard check, and the paper states which classes correspond. The contingency table is not public, and the displacing subset is small relative to the imaged cohort. The association cannot be recomputed, or its fragility checked, from open data.

operationalization: From real morphotype-1 cilia positions and beat directions, sum the propulsion vectors and compare the residual to measured displacement; alternatively, break the radial symmetry and ask whether wigglers start to translate. Near-zero net force on non-movers, and translation after symmetry is broken, would support cancellation; large residuals on bots that still do not move, or translation despite symmetric cilia, would point to another cause.
obstacles: Cilia coordinates and beat directions for morphotype 1 are not deposited.
Immobility is also explained by weak beat, adhesion or substrate friction.
An idealized sphere simulation would not be a test of these bots.
rationale: Force cancellation is a quantitative mechanics claim about the cilia actually on small spherical bots. Neither the masks nor the beat directions are public, so the vector sum cannot be run. Symmetry plus little movement is compatible with several causes, and separating them needs the missing geometry or a new perturbation.

operationalization: For each linear and circular bot, compute bilateral cilia symmetry about the movement axis and about the axis rotated 90 degrees, then repeat the paired rank test. Higher movement-axis symmetry in linear bots, and the opposite pattern in circular bots, would support distinct symmetry profiles; no axis difference would refute it.
obstacles: The test uses 15 circular and 13 linear bots, and the coordinates are not public.
The movement axis is taken from tracking, so symmetry and behavior are not independent measurements.
A reported p-value near 0.05 cannot be checked for leverage points without the pairs.
rationale: Symmetry about the movement axis versus a rotated axis is a concrete paired comparison, which is what the paper reports. The cilia coordinates for those 28 bots were not released. The contrast is informative in design and impossible to rerun until the points or a new paired sample exist.

operationalization: Bilateral symmetry of a straight-swimming spheroid is measurable, but 'recapitulating a fundamental property of wild-type species' and usefulness for studying embryonic midplanes do not state a result that would come out differently if the symmetry were only a physical consequence of moving in a line.
obstacles: Any elongated swimmer looks bilaterally symmetric about its path.
No homology, shared gene circuit or shared midplane mechanism is specified that could fail while the shape similarity remained.
rationale: Straight-line motion with mirror symmetry is a geometric description already covered by the symmetry measurements. Calling that pattern a recapitulation of animal bilateral organization, or a route into embryonic midplane formation, adds no observation that would distinguish it from ordinary mechanics of a ciliated spheroid. The statement is therefore not separable from its non-developmental reading.

operationalization: For bots on scratched neuronal monolayers, regress the fraction of unique positions visited along the scratch on rotational tendency and on speed. Positive slopes would support greater coverage by faster or more rotational bots; flat or negative slopes would refute it.
obstacles: The 17 tracked scratch trials are not deposited.
Speed and rotation can proxy bot size or tracking quality rather than coverage strategy.
Bots that never touched the scratch were excluded, so the sample is conditioned on interaction.
rationale: Coverage, rotation and speed are defined indices, and the paper gives slopes and sample size for the scratch trials. Those tracks are not public. The correlations are checkable in principle and confounded in practice, and neither the fit nor the confounds can be re-estimated from the published summary.

operationalization: On the pre-specified gyration window, fit scratch-edge similarity as a quadratic function of gyration and compare it with a linear fit on the same 13 bots. A quadratic improvement with an interior maximum would support an intermediate optimum; a linear or flat fit, or a maximum only at the boundary of the selected window, would refute it.
obstacles: The 13-bot subset was constrained to a gyration window after a linear fit misbehaved, and the points are not public.
A quadratic on 13 points is easy to overfit.
Edge similarity depends on how the scratch centerline was drawn.
rationale: A quadratic versus linear comparison of gyration against edge-tracking is a definite statistical claim. The paper reports p = 0.006 on a constrained set of 13 bots and does not release the points. With that sample size and with the model chosen after inspecting residuals, the open record cannot show whether an interior maximum is real.

operationalization: Place fused Anthrobot bridges across scratches in human neuronal monolayers and measure neuronal coverage under the bridge at 72 hours versus the same scratch without a bridge. Closure confined to the bridge, forming a stitch between the two sides, would support induction; no local regrowth, or regrowth everywhere along the scratch, would refute it.
obstacles: Replicate images and coverage values are not deposited; the paper reports that five of ten bridges stayed in place.
The neuronal cultures are one hiNSC differentiation protocol.
A stitch under the bot can be passive edge apposition rather than induced regrowth.
rationale: Local neuronal coverage at 72 hours under a superbot versus elsewhere on the scratch is a clear endpoint. The paper shows examples and states a qualitative regrowth result, with the images and measurements available on request. Example panels are not the replicate set, so the induction claim still needs the withheld images or a new scratch series.

operationalization: Binarize neuronal coverage under the bridge, in adjacent scratch, in distant scratch and in intact monolayer, and test equality with intact tissue and inequality with the rest of the scratch. Coverage under the bridge statistically matching intact tissue, and only there, would support full local recovery; a deficit under the bridge, or equal filling along the scratch, would refute it.
obstacles: Pixel densities after manual thresholding are not in a public table.
Statistical indistinguishability from 100% recovery depends on sample size and on the threshold.
The comparison uses the bridges that remained in place for three days.
rationale: Local coverage versus adjacent scratch and versus intact tissue is a defined density contrast. The paper reports full recovery under the bridge and lower coverage elsewhere, without depositing the region measurements. Manual thresholding makes the equality claim sensitive to choices that cannot be repeated from the summary alone.

operationalization: Incubate matched neuronal scratches for four days under agarose pieces sized like superbots and measure gap closure against superbot bridges and against empty scratches. No repair under agarose, with repair under bridges, would support the claim that passive mechanical loading is insufficient; closure under agarose would refute that negative result.
obstacles: The agarose control is a supporting figure, not a deposited coverage table.
Agarose stiffness, chemistry and contact area need not match a living bridge.
A single passive material does not exhaust mechanical explanations.
rationale: Gap closure under agarose versus under a living bridge is a direct negative-control contrast. The paper reports no repair and does not release the images or densities. One unmatched passive load is also a limited rival to contact mechanics, and neither the null result nor a better-matched control can be checked from open files.

operationalization: Recompute, from public Xenobot tracks and from Anthrobot tracks if released, the self-transition rates of circular and linear segments and the cross-transition rates between them. Overlapping very low linear-circular exchange and circular consistency near the reported 92–95% would support the shared profile; Xenobot rates far from 0.5–1.6% and 95%, once the same indices are used, would refute the Xenobot half.

candidate_datasets.name: Xenobots behavioral data and analysis code
candidate_datasets.role: raw tracks and R scripts for Xenobot movement types, from which transition rates can be recomputed if the same indices are applied

obstacles: Anthrobot segment labels are not in that repository.
Straightness and gyration as defined for Anthrobots may not match the Xenobot behavior features.
Similar transition percentages do not show that the two platforms share a mechanism.
rationale: A public Xenobot tracking archive and its analysis code can re-estimate movement-type persistence for the frog constructs, which is half of the numerical comparison. The Anthrobot percentages come from coordinates that were not released. Matching summary rates would still leave index definitions and biological interpretation only partly tested.

operationalization: Genomic distance between human and Xenopus, and similarity of the two motile spheroids, can both be measured. No outcome distinguishes 'generic laws of morphogenesis matter in addition to the genome' from both epithelia obeying the same packing and cilia mechanics in similar culture conditions.
obstacles: Morphological similarity of two ciliated spheroids is expected from shared culture physics without a further law.
The statement does not name a law, a prediction or a rival model that existing genomes or shapes could reject.
rationale: Human and frog genomes are obviously divergent, and both labs produced motile epithelial spheroids. That pair of facts does not separate a generic morphogenetic law from ordinary shared mechanics of ciliated epithelia. Nothing now public, and no reanalysis of genomes or shapes, would count as a confirmation or a refutation of the extra inference.

operationalization: Vary the number of bots per well in the days after matrix release and measure superbot size, and compare fusion rates while a basal marker is still on the surface versus after the surface is apical. Size scaling with bot number, and fusion restricted to the basal-exposed window, would support both clauses; size independent of number, or fusion after basal markers are covered, would refute them.
obstacles: Fusion counts versus bot number are not deposited.
Basal exposure is inferred from time since dissolution rather than from a paired basal-marker series.
Well crowding can change fusion without any special role for the basal surface.
rationale: Superbot size versus the number of input bots, and fusion versus basal-surface exposure, are both countable. The paper describes the control and the time window without releasing the counts or a basal-marker time series. Timing after dissolution is not itself a measurement of exposed basal layers, so the mechanism clause needs data that are not public.

operationalization: Whether tracheal-derived cells were observed over neural tissue is a factual report. 'Could not be predicted from any current model' and 'unexpected given normal roles' do not specify a model class, a prediction threshold or an observation that would fail if some existing model had entailed the interaction.
obstacles: Absence of a model from a database does not show that the outcome was unpredictable.
A model written after the experiment, or a model that was never formalized, both fit the wording.
rationale: The repair observation is an experimental report scored with the repair claims. The further statement that no current molecular or tissue model could have predicted it, and that this motivates a screen, is a judgment about the state of theory. No public analysis has a yes-or-no result that would confirm or refute unpredictability as stated.

operationalization: Implant Anthrobots made from a patient's own bronchial cells back into that patient, or into an autologous human explant with immune cells, and compare graft survival and T-cell or antibody responses with an allogeneic Anthrobot control. Absence of a response above the autologous-tissue baseline would support the safety claim; a raised response would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: Gene Expression Omnibus
candidate_datasets.role: public allogeneic-versus-autologous graft expression studies as a distant proxy; no Anthrobot implant series

obstacles: No public in vivo or immune-cell challenge of Anthrobots exists.
Culture-expanded autologous epithelium can still be immunogenic.
The statement is a future possibility, so a single negative explant would not establish clinical deployment.
rationale: Immune activation and graft survival after autologous versus allogeneic placement are standard endpoints. Nothing now public is an Anthrobot implant, and graft transcriptomes in general do not substitute for that exposure. The prediction is testable and currently lacks the data.

operationalization: Run the Anthrobot matrix-to-liquid protocol on adult human oviductal epithelium and on ependymal cells, and score external cilia and motility, and run it on a non-ciliated epithelial type scoring multicellular assembly without motility. Motile ciliated spheroids from the first two sources, and immotile spheroids from the third, would support the prediction; failure to form under the same protocol would refute it for those types.

candidate_datasets.name: CZ CELLxGENE
candidate_datasets.role: public single-cell expression showing ciliogenesis programs in oviductal epithelium and ependyma, not self-assembly or motility

obstacles: No public oviduct or ependymal run of the Anthrobot protocol exists.
Cilia-gene expression does not show that those cells will reverse polarity and swim.
Non-ciliated bots are an open-ended class rather than one tested type.
rationale: Formation and motility under the stated protocol are measurable for each named cell type. Public atlases show that oviduct and ependymal cells exist and express cilia genes; they do not contain the culture experiment. The prediction remains a new-experiment claim.

operationalization: That one human genome yields both airway epithelium and an Anthrobot anatomy in two environments can be granted from the culture result. 'Could affect the evolution of anatomical features' names no phylogenetic pattern, rate or fossil contrast that would confirm or refute an evolutionary effect.
obstacles: A modal claim that evolution could be affected is compatible with every phylogenetic outcome.
Environmental disclosure of epithelial mechanics does not, by itself, show a change in what selection sees.
rationale: The culture result shows one genome supporting more than one multicellular form. The evolutionary sentence only says that this capacity could matter for how anatomy evolves. No existing comparative or fossil analysis has a defined outcome that would establish or rule out that possibility.

operationalization: If the perceptual field is defined as the region of space and time a collective can survey, adding members enlarges that region by the definition used in the statement. No task, path metric or rival is given that would let 'improved search for variant paths' fail while the collective was still larger.
obstacles: Growth of a survey region with the number of sensors is stipulated rather than measured.
No dataset of cell collectives pairs group size with a count of alternative paths actually found.
rationale: The statement extends a definition of intelligence and then proposes that larger collectives survey more and therefore find more paths. Under that definition the first step does not come apart from 'more cells can sense more'. No observation is specified that would distinguish the proposal from that tautology.

operationalization: Date voltage-gated channels, gap-junction proteins and neurotransmitter machinery on metazoan and pre-metazoan genomes, and ask whether those families are present in non-neural lineages before the origin of neurons. Presence before neurons would support reuse of older components; restriction of the families to animals with nervous systems would weaken the temporal-order proxy. Neither result measures whether a neural self is a functional pivot of morphogenetic control.

candidate_datasets.name: Ensembl
candidate_datasets.role: comparative gene trees for ion channels, innexins or connexins, and neurotransmitter pathway genes across early-branching animals

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI GenBank
candidate_datasets.role: underlying sequences for the same families in sponges, placozoans, cnidarians and unicellular relatives

obstacles: Ancient shared components are compatible with co-option, convergence or unrelated reuse.
A centralized self, memories and goals are not variables in genome databases.
Gene presence is not evidence that the proteins controlled anatomy before they controlled behavior.
rationale: Public genomes can test the only sharply dated piece of the hypothesis: whether bioelectric components predate neurons. That analysis is standard and already feasible. It leaves the claim that neural unification into a self is an evolutionary pivot of morphogenetic problem-solving unmeasured, because component age does not establish homology of function.

operationalization: In avian blastoderms of one genotype, introduce temporary physical or informational breaks and count coherent embryos versus intact controls. More than one embryo after isolation of cell islands, and one embryo without the breaks, would support a genome that does not fix the count at one; a hard stop at one embryo despite complete separation would refute it.
obstacles: Embryo counts after blastoderm cuts live in classic experimental papers, not a deposited table.
Cuts confound informational isolation with loss of cells and with mechanical damage.
The published work is mostly chick, not blastoderms in general.
rationale: Embryo number after a defined separation is a direct count, and experimental twinning and triplet formation in the chick blastoderm is described with numbers in the developmental literature. Those counts are scattered in old papers rather than held as an open dataset. The contrast is informative for birds and incomplete for the full scope of embryonic blastoderms.

operationalization: In the same electric-field polarity, compute directedness of intact fish keratocytes and of their anucleate fragments, including field-reversal trials. Cathodal cells and anodal fragments, both reversing when the field reverses, would support opposite taxis; the same direction for fragments and cells would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: Sun et al. 2013, Current Biology
candidate_datasets.role: published trajectories, directedness means, field-reversal trials and movies for keratocytes versus fragments

obstacles: Raw tracks are in the paper and supplement, not a separate downloadable coordinate archive.
Retyping trajectories from figures is less precise than the original tracking files.
The result is for fish keratocytes, which is the claim's scope, but fragment preparation can select a biased subset of cytoplasm.
rationale: Direction relative to a defined field, with reversal controls, is a clean contrast, and the primary paper publishes trajectories, summary directedness and movies for both cells and fragments. That is scattered published measurement rather than an open tracking archive a third party can download and rerun. The opposite-taxis result can be re-measured from those materials with real limits on precision, which is a partial rather than a complete resolution.

operationalization: After a brief chloride-channel or GlyCl perturbation restricted to lineage-labeled instructor cells, score melanocyte number, ectopic location, arborization and vascular or neural invasion in the absence of an oncogene, and test whether a serotonergic block prevents the conversion. Conversion of distant melanocytes without those classical triggers, blocked by serotonin interference, would support the account; conversion only inside the labeled instructor region, or no serotonin dependence, would weaken it.

candidate_datasets.name: Xenbase
candidate_datasets.role: Xenopus phenotype and reagent records for instructor-cell and melanocyte experiments, not the raw image cohort

obstacles: Incidence counts and images are in the primary papers, not a deposited image set.
Hyperpigmentation can resemble a melanoma phenotype without a molecular diagnosis of melanoma.
Genome-wide absence of DNA damage was not the published assay; the claim is the lack of an applied carcinogen or oncogene.
rationale: Pigmentation extent, invasion and a serotonin rescue are measurable, and the instructor-cell papers report cohort incidences and images for chemical and GlyCl perturbations. Those files are not a public image archive, and Xenbase points at the experiments without holding the pixels. The phenotype can be checked against the published counts for this species, with the melanoma resemblance and the long-range mechanism only partly constrained.

operationalization: Score each tadpole as fully converted, fully normal or partial, under each reagent, and compare the within-animal pattern with a binomial model of independent melanocytes. All-or-none animals at varying cohort rates would support collective concordance. Re-implementing the published signaling model should then predict the drug and dominant-negative conditions under which partial animals appear; failure of those conditions, or partial animals in the original reagents, would refute the joint claim.

candidate_datasets.name: Xenbase
candidate_datasets.role: linked Xenopus literature and phenotypes for the conversion reagents, not per-animal melanocyte scores or model code

obstacles: Per-animal conversion scores and the model parameter file are not in a public repository.
Fully versus partially converted depends on a threshold applied to images.
It is unclear from the review alone whether the model equations are complete enough to re-run without the original code.
rationale: All-or-none scoring per animal, cohort incidence and a predicted partial-conversion intervention are all decidable if the per-animal table and the model are public. The review states the pattern and the successful prediction; the underlying scores and code are not an open deposit. A reanalysis can use the published incidences only as summaries, so both the concordance claim and the model confirmation stay partly out of reach. This was one of the harder items because model completeness cannot be judged from the review text alone.

operationalization: At a single planarian cut, record anterior-facing versus posterior-facing wound outcomes, and compare very short fragments or face-isolated tissue with fragments that retain long-range tissue. Opposite head and tail from one cut, lost when the fragment cannot communicate along its length, would support a non-local decision; correct polarity in an isolated wound face, or pre-existing molecular differences between the two faces, would allow a local account.

candidate_datasets.name: PlanMine
candidate_datasets.role: planarian gene expression and anatomy for anterior-posterior markers, not a table of fragment-polarity outcomes after cuts

obstacles: The two wound faces are not the same cells; local planar polarity can differ across a cut.
Short-fragment and double-head results are scattered across papers rather than one outcome table.
Correct polarity does not show that wound cells learn position in any sense beyond receiving a cue.
rationale: Head-versus-tail regeneration after one cut is among the most repeated observations in planarian biology, and very short or disrupted fragments are also widely reported. Those results live in many papers, while PlanMine holds markers rather than the cut outcomes. Opposite organs at one wound are real data, and they do not yet rule out local differences between the two faces, so the impossibility claim is only partly tested.

operationalization: After the stated bioelectric perturbations, score regenerates from the same parent as one-headed or two-headed and record whether any individual is a mosaic of head and tail tissue. A stable frequency near one double-headed animal in three, with each animal anatomically coherent, would support collective-level randomization; speckled identity within animals, or a ratio that is not repeatable, would refute the stated pattern.
obstacles: The roughly 1:2 counts are in the primary figures, not a multi-lab deposited table.
The ratio is tied to particular gap-junction or voltage perturbations and may not travel.
Coherent anatomy shows the outcome is animal-level; it does not show that a bioelectric variable was read by a collective rather than by a gradient.
rationale: Head number per fragment and within-animal coherence are directly scorable, and the source papers report a characteristic one-head to two-head frequency with coherent anatomy. Those counts are not a public raw table. The pattern can be checked from the published tallies for those perturbations, and the further reading that collectives interpret a randomized bioelectric state remains an inference from the absence of speckled tissue.

operationalization: Across published left-right perturbations, score whether each embryo's lateral markers are concordant (situs solitus, inversus or isomerism) or speckled within a side, and treat VANGL knockdown as the proposed exception. Finding speckled discs under other published treatments would refute uniqueness; concordant outcomes everywhere except the VANGL reports would support the survey claim as far as the sampled literature goes.

candidate_datasets.name: Xenbase
candidate_datasets.role: Xenopus gene and phenotype records for VANGL and left-right markers, as an index into the published perturbation literature

obstacles: Concordant situs classes are what papers usually score, so speckling can be under-reported.
The survey is bounded by studies the authors know, not by a pre-registered sample.
Marker speckles can be staining noise rather than cells disagreeing about identity.
rationale: Within-embryo concordance of left-right markers is visible in a large published in situ literature, and Xenbase indexes the Xenopus share of it, including VANGL. Extracting speckling versus isomerism across that literature is weeks to months of figure scoring, not a download of one table. Publication bias and an open-ended study list keep the 'only one perturbation' clause only partly decidable.

operationalization: Compare Hox or reporter expression of single neural-crest or rhombomere cells grafted to a new axial level with expression of coherent groups grafted to the same level. Groups keeping donor expression while isolated cells matching the host would support the contrast; both classes changing, or both keeping donor identity, would refute it. A longer 'perceptual field' is not a further measurement beyond that retention.

candidate_datasets.name: Trainor and Krumlauf 2000, Nature Cell Biology
candidate_datasets.role: published mouse grafts of small rhombomere groups versus dispersed cells, with Hox reporter and lineage label

obstacles: Graft size, dispersion and cell survival are entangled in the classic experiments.
Counts are in figures from mouse, chick and zebrafish papers, not one deposited cell table.
Maintained gene expression does not measure memory duration or a perceptual field extending into the past.
rationale: Donor versus host Hox expression after single-cell versus group grafts is a defined contrast, and the mouse transposition paper publishes it with lineage labels. Related chick and zebrafish grafts are separate papers, not a combined open count matrix. The expression difference can be re-examined from those figures for a few vertebrates, while the memory and perceptual-field gloss is not an additional variable in the data.
